design:
D1 Amendments live in spec_amendments. It already owns the only post-approval change path, as Hub-owned append-only events with the structural operations (spec_amendments.py:223 apply, :348 amend). A proposal is an `amendment_proposed` event carrying the operation; acceptance runs `apply` on the document as it stands and writes through `spec_service._apply_and_write`, recording the existing `amendment` event (with `proposal` naming the proposal) and its review in one step, so every reader of amendments (counts, unreviewed_relaxing, the panel) keeps working; decline is an `amendment_declined` event. SpecEditProposal (whole-unit payload diffs, D1-D3 of the 2026 rigor change) is not reused: it diffs whole requirements against a digest, and two accepted proposals would overwrite each other where operations do not. New op `add_requirement` (key, statement, modal, rationale), since an added task must trace to a requirement. Who proposes: agents with a `content` event before `first_approved_at`, and the lead of the document's running build (builds.py); the tester keeps `amend` (non-goals). The operator decides; the proposer is told through queue_note_to_reporter (spec_amendments.py:868).

D2 An accepted task joins a build through spec_tasks.materialise, which already attaches a new task to the document's live loop (spec_tasks.py:281, :420); slice D's builds.join_running_build adds the build, its level and the declared builder, and flow_advance wakes the driver.

D3 Rigor retires in whole. Its proposals half is redundant once slice C keeps exploring documents editable and refuses a stale approval; its evidence half is slice D's level. Removed: the propose branch (spec_service.py:231-234), the routes (api/v1/spec.py:768 rigor, :938 rigor-history, :1261-1388 proposals), the app's control and proposals panels, rigor in the stored hub block and the rendered document. requirement_gate's per-document rule becomes the task's level, sketch's rule when there is none. Kept: the rigor column, spec_rigor_events and spec_edit_proposals, unread. spec_rigor keeps policy_digest, which requirement_gate uses.

D4 The main watch is a new module, main_watch.py, called from project_checks.watch_main_once (one 30-second poll, project_checks.py:75, :1282) for every project with a main branch; the check refresh stays project_checks'. Own merges are recognised by sha, not by author or message: integrate records `merged_sha` (HEAD after `git merge --no-ff`, task_integration.py:793-816) on the TaskIntegration row, and a move is the Hub's when every first-parent commit from the seen tip is a recorded merged_sha. Identity cannot do it: the Hub's snapshots on task branches carry the same committer identity (worktrees.py:60), so a fast-forward of an agent's branch would pass. The seen tip is persisted on the project (`main_tip_seen`) so a restart neither loses nor re-raises a move; a null seen tip records without raising.

D5 Hand merges are raised. The operator's interactive commits and the orchestrator's merges of this roadmap's work go to master by hand, and nothing reliable tells them from an agent's commit made in the main checkout: an exemption a commit can carry (a trailer, an author) is one an agent can write. So they are raised, and made cheap: one open notice per project gathers every move until marked seen, listing each commit's sha, subject and author, so the operator recognises their own merges at a glance. Not a stall: stalls wake the mender (stalls.py:168-177), which cannot act on this.

D6 The offer is derived, not stored: a slice document is offered when it has no open task, the roadmap's next slice is claimed by no document, and no `next_slice_queued` or `next_slice_declined` event answers it. Deriving needs no data migration, and an earlier unanswered `next_slice_requested` (one on :8000) shows as an offer by the same rule. on_task_closed (slice_drafting.py:135) notifies instead of queueing. Taking reuses _queue_if_built's body (the turn text with outcomes, F501; the open-or-new conversation, F1047, slice_drafting.py:203-218; the queued event as the once guard), with the agent chosen by the operator.

Hazard (Tier 2). Two migrations on the live database. Rigor migration: open tasks of contract/gate documents outside a build get level reviewed/gated; pending edit proposals become stale with a reason; downgrade sets those levels back to null and the proposals back to pending (rows identified by the reason). Main-watch migration: task_integrations.merged_sha, projects.main_tip_seen, a main_notices table; downgrade drops them. On :8000 (read-only, 2026-10-27): all documents sketch, 0 proposals, 2 projects with a main branch, so the rigor backfill changes no row and the first look raises nothing. Back up :8000 with the sqlite backup API first. The watch now runs git every 30 s for each project with a main branch, not only those with checks: two on :8000.

problem:
- After approval only a tester can change a document (`spec_amendments.amend` refuses everyone else: 'only a run testing a task of this document may amend it', hub/hub/spec_amendments.py:381-388), and its change applies at once. A lead or the author that finds a missing task mid-build has no way to add it except asking the operator to reopen the document. Operator, 2026-10-26: after approval the author and the lead propose amendments and the operator accepts them.
- Document rigor mixes two things: at contract/gate an agent's save becomes an edit proposal (`spec_service.save_document`, hub/hub/spec_service.py:231-234), and at gate approval needs accepted evidence (requirement_gate.py:1217-1228). Slice C makes exploring documents freely editable and refuses a stale approval, and slice D moves the evidence rule into the build's level, so the setting no longer decides anything a build does not. On :8000 every one of 180 documents is sketch and there are 0 edit proposals (read-only query, 2026-10-27): the machinery is unused.
- Main moving outside the Hub is noticed only to refresh check results: `watch_main_once` polls every 30 s (project_checks.py:75, :1282-1299), only for projects with checks, keeps the last tip in memory (`_seen_tips`, :884) and tells nobody. 23-25 October recorded agents touching the main checkout; the roadmap's answer is that the Hub notices and raises it, never blocks it (operator, 2026-10-26).
- The next slice's drafting is requested at approval (`draft_next_slice`, hub/hub/api/v1/spec.py:3244-3251, :3403-3407) and queued automatically when the last task closes (slice_drafting.py:135-152). On 2026-10-27 at 05:44 slice B's drafting turn was queued to the Architect while the operator was asleep and the roadmap was being reworked by hand; one request from 2026-10-25 (the-app-stays-responsive-while-agents-run) is still unanswered on :8000. The operator wants to decide when, and by whom, the next slice is drafted.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26. 'Author' is every agent with a content save before first approval, not the creator: 159 of 180 documents on :8000 were created by the operator and written by an agent (read-only query of spec_document_events, 2026-10-27).
requirements.statement: After a document is approved, an agent that wrote its content before approval, or the lead of its running build, can propose an amendment to it (add a task, add a requirement, add, change or remove a criterion) with a reason and how to check it; the proposal changes neither the document nor the board until the operator accepts it; any other agent's proposal is refused, naming who may propose.

requirements.rationale: Re-applying the structural operation at acceptance, rather than a stored whole-document diff, keeps two accepted amendments from overwriting each other.
requirements.statement: The operator sees each proposed amendment on its document with its author, reason, how to check it and the change it makes; accepting applies it to the document as it stands then and records it as accepted by the operator, or is refused as stale, naming why, when the change no longer applies; declining records the operator's reason; the proposer receives the decision as input in either case.

A task added by an accepted amendment joins the document's running build at once, carrying that build and its level and its declared builder, and its driver hands it out like any other task of the build; with no build running it waits on the board and joins the next build started on the document.
Before approval, every save of a document by an agent or the operator is applied directly, whatever rigor the document carried; no edit proposal is created.

requirements.rationale: The backfill keeps a stricter document's open work from loosening silently on another install; on :8000 it touches no row.
requirements.statement: No route, tool or control in the app sets or shows a document's rigor; approval's evidence rule comes from the task's level (slice D), and a task outside any build is judged by sketch's rule unless it records a level; when this ships, each open task of a contract or gate document outside a build records reviewed or gated respectively, and each pending edit proposal is marked stale with a reason naming the retirement.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26: notice and raise, never block. Hand merges by the operator and the orchestrator are raised too (design D5).
requirements.statement: Within 60 seconds of a project's main branch tip moving by any commit other than a merge the Hub's own integration made, the operator receives a notification and sees an Overview notice naming the commits (short sha, subject, author) and the old and new tip; a move that rewrote history (the old tip no longer an ancestor) is raised as a rewrite; nothing is blocked, reverted or retried because of it.
A move made only of merge commits the Hub recorded making when it integrated approved work raises nothing.

requirements.rationale: The operator commits to master by hand most days; one notice per unseen stretch keeps that from becoming a pile.
requirements.statement: Moves raised while a main notice is still unseen are added to it rather than raising another; marking it seen closes it; the tip last accounted for survives a Hub restart, so a move made while the Hub was down is raised at its first look, and the very first look after this ships records the tip without raising anything.

When the last open task of a document that specifies a roadmap slice closes and the roadmap's following slice is claimed by no document, the operator is notified and offered that slice's drafting on the Overview and the document's page; no drafting turn is queued until the operator takes the offer.

Taking the offer queues one drafting turn, carrying the slice's outcomes as today's turn does, to the agent the operator chooses (by default the document's author), in the conversation where the document was written while it is open and otherwise in a new one (F1047); declining it hides it for that slice; approval no longer accepts a request to draft the next slice, refusing it by name, and a request recorded before this ships shows as an offer.

in_scope: Amendment proposals after approval by the document's authors and the lead of its running build: add a task, add a requirement, add, change or remove a criterion
The operator accepting (applied then, or refused as stale) or declining with a reason, the proposer told either way
An accepted task joining the running build, or waiting for the next one
Retiring the rigor setting: exploring saves always apply, edit proposals end, the routes and the app's rigor control and proposals panel go

A main watch over every project with a main branch, persisting the tip it last saw, raising moves that are not the Hub's own merges within a minute, coalesced into one notice until the operator marks it seen
The next slice's drafting offered when a slice's work is built, taken by the operator with the agent of their choice, F1047's new-conversation behaviour kept
non_goals: The tester's amendments (applied at once, reviewed afterwards, spec_amendments.py:1-19): unchanged; a tester that finds a gap while testing keeps the build moving, and its relaxing amendments already hold their requirement unverifiable until the operator reviews them
Amending a requirement's statement after approval: that is a reopen, as today
Blocking or reverting a move of main: the Hub raises it and nothing else (roadmap non-goal)
Telling the operator's or the orchestrator's own hand merges apart from an agent's: they are raised too, and recognised by the commits listed in the notice (design D5)
Dropping the rigor column or the spec_edit_proposals table: both stay, unread; dropping is an SQLite table rebuild for no behaviour
Drafting the next slice automatically: the offer replaces it
The mender: a main move or an offer is not a stall and wakes nobody (slice N owns the mender)
The redesigned spec page: slice F; amendments and offers appear on today's header and panel

summary: Three things that follow a build (slice D) and finish roadmap slice D. After approval, the document's author and the lead of its running build propose amendments, which change nothing until the operator accepts them; an accepted one that adds a task puts it in the running build, or on the board for the next one. Document rigor retires: before approval edits apply directly, after approval they are amendments, and how strictly evidence is judged is the build's level. The Hub watches the main branch and raises, within a minute, any move that is not its own integration merge, without blocking anything. And when a roadmap slice's work is built, drafting the next slice is offered to the operator rather than queued, and starts only when they take the offer.
